title: Aeration Deficit
publisher: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program
scope: Root-zone oxygen supply, waterlogging, root respiration, water and nutrient uptake, chronic saturation, root decline, and the overlap between aeration deficit and root-decay pathogens.

title: Water Deficit and Excess
publisher: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program
scope: Plant injury from insufficient or excessive root-zone moisture, irrigation diagnosis, overwatering, poor drainage, aeration deficit, and the need to distinguish wet-root and dry-root stress.

title: Drowning and Edema
scope: Non-infectious edema symptoms, lower-leaf blisters and corking, excess moisture, humid conditions, and water uptake exceeding transpiration.

title: Phytotoxicity: Chemical Damage to Garden Plants
scope: Chemical and pesticide injury, spray-pattern damage, spotting, scorch, distortion, look-alikes, exposure history, and clues that distinguish one-time phytotoxic injury from pests and infectious disease.

title: Herbicide Damage on Vegetables
scope: Off-target herbicide injury, drift, distorted and strappy new growth, multi-species exposure clues, symptom timing, and differential diagnosis against cultural, insect, mite, disease, and virus problems.

title: Saline Soils and Plant Growth
scope: Soluble-salt accumulation, electrical-conductivity measurement, method-dependent EC interpretation, greenhouse and high-tunnel salt risk, root-zone leaching, and plant response to salinity.

title: A Water Quality Toolkit for Greenhouse and Nursery Production
scope: Greenhouse water-quality monitoring, pH, alkalinity, hardness, electrical conductivity, meter calibration, recordkeeping, and the relationship between irrigation chemistry, growing-media pH, and nutrient availability.

title: Potting Media and Plant Propagation
scope: Greenhouse soilless-media testing, saturated-media methods, pH, soluble salts, nutrient analysis, media aeration, drainage, and propagation-root-zone quality.

title: Chilling Injury in Newly Planted Corn and Soybeans
scope: General crop chilling-injury principles, cold and wet root-zone exposure, low-temperature stress around germination and establishment, and the importance of temperature history when interpreting injury.
